attributes.description:
Sets the background color of lists (containers that hold multiple list items in a vertical or horizontal arrangement). This is the main background color that appears behind the list container.
CSS variable: --wm-list-background

Controls the minimum height of lists (containers that hold multiple list items). This ensures the list is always tall enough to be visible and properly displayed, even when it has few items.
CSS variable: --wm-list-min-height

Controls the transparency of lists (containers that hold multiple list items). When set to 1, the list is fully opaque. Lower values make the list more transparent, higher values make it more opaque.
CSS variable: --wm-list-opacity

Controls whether list items can receive mouse/touch interactions. 'all' makes list items fully interactive (clickable, hoverable), 'none' makes them ignore all mouse/touch events (like they're invisible to the mouse), and 'auto' lets the browser decide. This is useful for enabling/disabling list functionality.
CSS variable: --wm-list-pointer-events

Sets the color of the state layer that appears when users hover, focus, or interact with list items. This creates visual feedback to show that the list item is interactive and responsive to user actions.
CSS variable: --wm-list-state-layer-color

Controls the transparency of the state layer that appears during user interactions with list items (hover, focus, active). When set to 0, the state layer is invisible. Higher values make the interaction feedback more visible.
CSS variable: --wm-list-state-layer-opacity

Sets the background color of list items (individual entries in a list that users can interact with). This is the main background color that appears behind each list item content.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-background

Controls the thickness of the border around list items. When set to 0, there's no visible border. Higher values create thicker borders around each list item.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-border-width

Sets the color of the border around list items. This creates a colored border to define the boundaries of each list item.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-border-color

Sets the border style of list items. Acceptable values: solid, dashed, dotted.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-border-style

Controls the corner rounding of list items. When set to 'none', list items have sharp corners. Higher values create more rounded corners.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-border-radius

Controls the box shadow (elevation) of list items. This determines the shadow depth and visual elevation of a list item above the list background.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-box-shadow

Controls the internal spacing inside list items (the space between the list item content and its borders). This creates breathing room around each list item content.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-padding

Controls the internal spacing inside list item headers (section titles that group related list items). This creates breathing room around the header text.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-header-padding

Sets the background color of list item headers (section titles that group related list items). This is the main background color that appears behind the header text.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-header-background

Sets the text color of list item headers (section titles that group related list items). This determines what color the header text appears in, which should contrast well with the background for readability.
CSS variable: --wm-list-item-header-color

Sets the color of the outline around list elements (containers that hold multiple list items). This creates a colored border around the list to define its boundaries.
CSS variable: --wm-list-border-color

Controls the thickness of the outline around list elements. When set to 0, there is no visible border. Higher values create thicker borders around the list.
CSS variable: --wm-list-border-width

Controls the style of the outline around list elements. 'none' removes the border, 'solid' creates a continuous line, 'dashed' creates a dashed line, 'dotted' creates small dots.
CSS variable: --wm-list-border-style

Controls the corner rounding of list elements. When set to 'none', lists have sharp corners. Higher values create more rounded corners for a softer appearance.
CSS variable: --wm-list-border-radius

Controls the drop shadow effect around list elements. This creates a subtle shadow that makes the list appear to float above the background, giving it depth and elevation.
CSS variable: --wm-list-shadow

Disables mouse/touch interactions for disabled list items. When set to 'none', disabled list items ignore all mouse/touch events, making them completely non-interactive. This prevents users from clicking or hovering over disabled items.
CSS variable: --wm-list-pointer-events (disabled state)
